verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI's first-party multi-agent guide documents three orchestration patterns inside one application: agent delegation (an agent calls another agent via tools, then takes back control), programmatic agent hand-off (application code calls the next agent), and graph-based control flow. Its evals docs also explicitly target 'complex multi-agent applications'. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-agent workflows, and deeper evidence beyond the guide's summary snippets (e.g. shared state or usage across delegated agents, crew-style role teams).

support.subject: As a developer, I can orchestrate multiple agents — handoffs, subagents, or crews — inside one workflow

citations.quote: Agent delegation — agents using another agent via tools... Programmatic agent hand-off — one agent runs, then application code calls another agent... Graph based control flow
"Agent delegation" refers to the scenario where an agent delegates work to another agent, then takes back control when the delegate agent ... finishes.
from simple LLM calls to complex multi-agent applications
